Docs.summary: Initializes a new instance of seeded from a prior durable snapshot for a crash-recovery re-invocation. The recovered handler passes so the resumed stream continues from the output items already emitted before the crash rather than restarting: the seeded response's output items are retained and the output-index allocator is advanced to persistedResponse.Output.Count so new AddOutputItem* calls do not collide with the already-emitted slots (mirrors Python's ResponseEventStream(response=...) recovery branch). Emit (idempotent on recovery) then as the client-visible reset carrying the seeded output.

Public Overridable Function CreateCheckpointEvent () As ResponseStreamEvent

abstract member CreateCheckpointEvent : unit -> Azure.AI.AgentServer.Responses.Models.ResponseStreamEvent override this.CreateCheckpointEvent : unit -> Azure.AI.AgentServer.Responses.Models.ResponseStreamEvent

Docs.summary:
Produces a checkpoint control signal to yield at a phase boundary so the framework persists the current snapshot as a resume watermark.
It is a pure factory: the returned event has no effect until the handler yields it — yield return stream.CreateCheckpointEvent();. The yield is backpressured — control does not return to the handler until the persist completes. The checkpoint is a no-op unless the response is a resilient background response (ResilientBackground=true + store=true + background=true). On recovery, is hydrated from the last successful checkpoint, so an idempotent handler resumes from its last phase rather than restarting.
The signal is never emitted to the SSE wire; it does not consume a sequence number.
Docs.returns: A checkpoint control event to yield for persistence.

Docs.summary: Gets the framework-reserved metadata map that is persisted with the response for recovery and stripped on egress — the .NET equivalent of Python's stream.internal_metadata. Unlike (the client's own metadata, which is never stripped), every mutation here is folded into the response snapshot as a compact JSON string under the reserved key _internal_metadata inside , so it is persisted with the response on every snapshot the orchestrator writes and survives crash/recovery (read back on recovery via ). It is stripped from every client-facing ingress/egress payload by . Keys are free-form; values are strings. On a mock-constructed stream (no backing response) the map is purely in-memory.
